Microsoft durabletask PyPI hit by Mini Shai-Hulud

Target: durabletask · website · repo
Date: 2026-05-19
Actor: TeamPCP (group)
Target Kind: library
Language: Python
Cause: compromised_account_credentials
Motive: credential_theft_data_exfiltration
Transitive: true
Impact: credential_theft, data_exfiltration, self_propagation, destruction
User Impact: 0
Phase: distribution
Campaigns: Shai-Hulud hits npm and PyPI

Synopsis

TeamPCP published malicious durabletask 1.4.1, 1.4.2, and 1.4.3 to PyPI with a stolen token, bypassing Microsoft's CI/CD path. The dropper fetched rope.pyz to harvest cloud and password-manager credentials, spread via AWS SSM and kubectl, and conditionally wiped disks.

Story

Microsoft's `durabletask` is the official Python SDK for Azure Durable Functions. It receives roughly 400,000 PyPI downloads per month. On 2026-05-19 TeamPCP published three malicious versions, 1.4.1, 1.4.2, and 1.4.3, in a 35-minute window. A GitHub issue and an Amazon Inspector advisory triggered Microsoft to yank them. None of the three versions had a matching tag, release, or CI/CD run in `microsoft/durabletask-python`. The attacker had reached the registry directly with a stolen publishing credential and bypassed the project's GitHub path. Wiz traced the credential to a contributor account previously seen in the @antv wave. The attacker copied the latest legitimate commit message to mask the upload and pulled the PyPI token from GitHub repository secrets.

Each version pushed the dropper deeper into the package. 1.4.1 patched `__init__.py`. 1.4.2 added `task.py`. 1.4.3 spread the dropper across `entities/`, `extensions/`, and `payload/` `__init__.py` files. The fourteen-line dropper ran at import time on Linux and fetched a 28 KB second stage, `rope.pyz`, from `check.git-service.com`, a domain registered three days earlier via NameSilo. rope.pyz collected from ninety-plus on-disk credential paths covering AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, GitHub, Docker, SSH, Terraform/Ansible/Pulumi state, shell histories, AI tool configs for Claude, Cursor, VS Code MCP, and Codeium, and the 1Password, Bitwarden, pass, and gopass CLIs. Persistence wrote `/tmp/managed.pyz`, installed a `pgsql-monitor.service` systemd unit, and marked infected hosts with `~/.cache/.sys-update-check`.

Propagation followed TeamPCP's other 2026 waves. The payload ran AWS SSM `SendCommand` against up to five EC2 instances per harvested profile and `kubectl exec` into up to five pods per discovered cluster. Exfiltration ran three parallel channels: HTTPS POST to the C2, GitHub commit beacons under the `FIRESCALE` tag using victim tokens, and public repositories created on stolen GitHub accounts under the Russian-folklore names BABA-YAGA, KOSCHEI, FIREBIRD, RUSALKA, MOROZKO, and LESHY. Evasion was minimal. The payload skipped Russian-locale systems, skipped hosts with two or fewer CPU cores, and redirected output to `/dev/null`. A `roulette.py` module inspected locale settings for Israeli and Iranian targets and, when matched, played an audio file and ran `rm -rf /*` with a one-in-six probability.

Amazon Inspector flagged the packages as MAL-2026-4174. A public report landed in `microsoft/durabletask-python` issue #137 at 17:54 UTC. Microsoft yanked all three versions ten minutes later. Shared `t.m-kosche.com` infrastructure and the folklore-naming pattern tied the operation to TeamPCP's Mini Shai-Hulud activity, even though durabletask was PyPI rather than npm and the payload was a Python pyz rather than the `@tanstack/setup` Node module from the May 11 wave. The cross-ecosystem aggregate lives on [[shai-hulud-here-we-go-again]]. This record holds the durabletask-specific evidence.
